stages.name: base
stages.text:
Build a per-user sliding-window rate limiter.
Input (stdin, one JSON object): {"limit": int >= 0, "window": int >= 1, "events": [{"t": int, "user": string}, ...]}. Events are sorted by t (non-decreasing); equal t values are processed in list order.
A request by user u at time t is allowed when fewer than `limit` earlier ALLOWED requests by u have a time in the half-open interval (t - window, t]. Denied requests never count.
Output (stdout, one JSON object): {"allowed": [bool, ...]} with one entry per event, in input order.

stages.name: cr1
stages.text: Change request 1: the input may carry an optional field "overrides": {user: int >= 0}. A user listed there uses that limit instead of the global `limit`. Users not listed keep the global limit.

stages.name: cr2
stages.text: Change request 2: the output must also contain "denied": {user: int} giving, for each user with at least one denied request, how many of their requests were denied. Users with no denials do not appear.

reqs.text: allowed iff fewer than limit allowed requests by the same user in (t-window, t]
denied requests do not count toward the window
limit 0 denies everything; empty events gives empty list
per-user override replaces the global limit for that user only
denied map counts denials per user; users without denials absent

mutants.m2: denied requests count toward the window
mutants.m3: denied map includes users with zero denials
